title: substrate ablation — load-bearing component identification for the H_204 closure inverse-U finding (/gap F2)
hypothesis: the H_204 closure inverse-U finding (Φ(k) peaks at interior k; C4 threshold; F1 intact) separates substrate components into load-bearing vs non-essential under one-at-a-time ablation
honest_tier: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL (phi_spatial proxy + ablation sweep; NOT 🔵 formal IIT 4.0)
phi_primitive: RFC 036 phi_spatial (n_bins=4); H_204 / H_003 H3.4 byte-equal carry
model: 8-site periodic catalytic lattice (H_204 carry); one-at-a-time ablation of {diffusion, decay, michaelis-saturation, closure-coupling}
survival_criterion: finding SURVIVES iff S1 (argmax Φ at interior k) AND S2 (peak|ΔΦ/Δk|>2×median) AND S3 (Φ(k=1)>Φ(k=0)); component LOAD-BEARING iff ablation BREAKS finding
mitosis_components_scope_note: task vocabulary {split, merge, gaussian-noise} are MITOSIS-substrate components (tool/hexa_native/mitosis_hook_lib.hexa), NOT present in the H_204 catalytic-lattice substrate. The H_204 finding is deterministic with zero gaussian draws (baseline byte-equal re-run). These three are trivially non-essential to this finding (never invoked). The four ablated arms are the components the finding actually depends on.
verdict_rule: SUPPORTED iff (baseline reproduces H_204) AND C1 AND C2 AND C3; FALSIFIED if all non-essential OR all load-bearing OR determinism fail
honest_limits: L1: phi_spatial = 🟢 NUMERICAL spatial-slice replica of phi_rs, NOT full IIT 4.0. H_204 / H_003 H3.4 lineage carry.

L2: ablation = neutralization within ONE substrate family (single-parameter zeroing / saturation-drop / closure-flattening). Other neutralization parametrizations (partial diffusion, sigmoid saturation) would give graded survival, not the binary survive/break used here.

L3: survival is a 3-clause boolean (S1∧S2∧S3) on a COARSE 6-point k grid (H_204 L4 carry). A finer grid could shift argmax between adjacent interior points without changing the interior/endpoint distinction, but a near-endpoint argmax is grid-resolution sensitive.

L4: WINDOW-SENSITIVE (H_204 L3 / H_003 H3.4 L3 carry). All Φ measured on the WARM=0 DIM=12 living transient; past convergence Φ→~0 for all arms. Load-bearing classification is a transient-window claim.

L5: {split, merge, gaussian-noise} are mitosis-substrate components absent from this finding's substrate; their 'non-essential' status here is by-absence (the finding never invokes them), NOT a measured ablation on a substrate that uses them. A separate cycle would ablate them against a mitosis-substrate finding (e.g. F-PERSONA / Φ-proxy ratchet).

L6: one-at-a-time ablation does not test interactions — two jointly-load-bearing components could each individually appear non-essential (redundancy) or jointly break when each alone survives. Factorial ablation is a future cycle.

L7: determinism here is in-process byte-equal across re-eval; full cross-process determinism (RFC 033 single global RNG stream caveat) is asserted via result.json sha256 comparison across two separate `hexa run` invocations — recorded in the doc, not self-checked in-process.
